name: Australian Capital Territory

gate.mechanism: Most food businesses must register with the Health Protection Service before opening. Access Canberra is the application portal. Registration terms of 1, 2 or 3 years are available. Premises are inspected before registration is granted. Domestic home kitchens are approved for low-risk foods only.
gate.fee_notes: Risk-based published schedule: low/medium/high × 1/2/3 years. Low risk 1 year A$163; medium A$239.50; high A$321.55 (ACT fees page and registration form, retrieved 2026-08-24). Some service/charitable organisations may be fee-exempt with evidence.
gate.change_of_details_rule: Food Act s 97 requires notice of change in registration details or operation; confirm current form with HPS.

licence_exemptions: Limited occasions: ≤5 periods/year, each ≤3 days, and food is either non-potentially hazardous unpackaged or sold straight after thorough cooking for immediate consumption (Food Regulation; ACT register guidance)
Sells only closed-package non-potentially hazardous food
Food transport vehicle registered under corresponding State law
Transports food only (no other handling or sale)
Vending machine selling only non-potentially hazardous food

channels.render_reason: No ACT channel-by-channel rulebook published; prose explains Act coverage and absence of honesty-box exemption
channels.notes: Food Act s 10 covers commercial, charitable, community and single-occasion activity. No published honesty-box exemption. Declared events require registration.

labelling.basis: Australia New Zealand Food Standards Code (labelling standards); country of origin under ACL Information Standard 2016
required_elements: Supplier name and street address in Australia or New Zealand
Best-before or use-by date where required
Directions for use and storage where required
Warning and advisory statements, and allergen declaration
labelling.allergen_rule: Allergen declaration required as a Code label element where applicable (Standard 1.2.3)

training.fss_trigger: Registered food businesses must nominate an appropriately trained Food Safety Supervisor. ACT guidance notes some non-profit community organisations are exempt from the FSS requirement. Confirm with HPS.

premises.inspection_frequency_basis: Premises inspected by ACT Health before registration is granted. Public health officers may also inspect later at any reasonable time. Domestic kitchens: low-risk / shelf-stable preparation only.
premises.construction_standard: Standard 3.2.3; ACT Food Business Fit-out Guide
exemptions_never_granted_for: Medium or high-risk food preparation in a domestic home kitchen (ACT home-based guidance and registration form: only shelf-stable low-risk food unless separate approved commercial kitchen)

food_safety_management.standard_322a_trigger: Applies nationally to Category 1 and Category 2 food service, catering and retail businesses handling unpackaged, potentially hazardous ready-to-eat food.

unique.quirk_paragraph: The ACT looks like a single-gate registration system, but kitchen suitability is a second gate. Domestic home kitchens are approved only for low-risk, shelf-stable preparation. Higher-risk food needs a separate approved commercial kitchen. Registration exemptions for limited occasions or closed-package non-potentially hazardous sales remove the registration obligation only; they do not create a cottage-food regime or remove food safety law. Growing food can sit outside registration; selling it directly to the public does not stay inside the primary-production definition.
unique.common_mistake: Assuming a local council handles ACT food-business registration, or assuming a domestic kitchen can be registered for any food type once the fee is paid.
unique.what_does_not_apply: There is no ACT municipal-council food-registration pathway. There is no US-style cottage food approved list or sales cap. Some non-profit organisations may be exempt from the Food Safety Supervisor requirement; confirm with HPS.

information_gain: Territory gate: HPS registration before opening; Access Canberra is the portal, not a council
Home kitchens approved for low-risk / shelf-stable preparation only; higher-risk needs separate commercial kitchen
Published risk-based fee schedule including low-risk 1-year A$163
Narrow registration exemptions (≤5×/year ≤3 days with food-type limits; closed-package non-PHF) still require food safety compliance
Primary production excludes direct sale or service to the public (Food Act s 11)
s 89 maximum: 50 penalty units, 6 months imprisonment, or both; penalty unit currently A$160 individual / A$810 corporation
